note: THE CHECK NOBODY HAD RUN. Rendered the swallowtail out of BF-01 (flight camera, same renderer, same halftone) and the old butterfly out of BF-24 (mark azimuth) and read them side by side at matched wing size. VERDICT: same species, different picture. Carried across: the forewing's produced apex and long costal margin, the hindwing lobe and tail, the radiating venation from a wing root, the clubbed antenna, the level-2 membrane. Broken: the silhouette. Four wings around a vertical body becomes two wings over a horizontal one; the eyes vanish (they are authored in the Z=0 plane and go edge-on) and the antennae splay to one side of the head instead of framing it. This is a real cost. It is affordable because BF-27 — 'This one has the same marking' — is on the flight camera and is untouched, and because the marking itself, which is what that line is about, is the thing this camera makes legible.
